proposals.before: Her eldest brother, Marquis Lü of Zhou, died on campaign. His son Lü Tai was enfeoffed as Marquis of Li, and his son Zichan as Marquis of Jiao;
proposals.after: Her eldest brother, Marquis Lü of Zhou, died on campaign. His son Lü Tai was enfeoffed as Marquis of Li, and his son Chan as Marquis of Jiao;
proposals.reason: In 子產為交侯, 子 means son and 產 is the given name (Lü Chan), not the fused personal name Zichan.

proposals.before: The remainder were all Emperor Xiaohui's younger brothers. Concubine Qi's son Ruyi was the King of Zhao. Lady Bo's son Heng was the King of Dai. The other consorts' sons were Zihui, King of Liang; Ziyou, King of Huaiyang; Zichang, King of Huainan; and Zijian, King of Yan.
proposals.after: The remainder were all Emperor Xiaohui's younger brothers. Concubine Qi's son Ruyi was the King of Zhao. Lady Bo's son Heng was the King of Dai. The other consorts' sons were Hui, King of Liang; You, King of Huaiyang; Chang, King of Huainan; and Jian, King of Yan.
proposals.reason: In 子恢/子友/子長/子建, 子 means son; given names are 恢/友/長/建. Zihui-style forms incorrectly fuse kinship 子 into the name.

proposals.before: At dawn, Emperor Xiaohui returned. The King of Zhao was already dead.
proposals.after: By dawn, Emperor Xiaohui had returned; the King of Zhao was already dead.
proposals.reason: 犁明 marks the coming of dawn as the frame when Xiaohui returned to find Ruyi already dead.

proposals.before: On xinchou in the ninth month, she was buried.
proposals.after: On xinchou in the ninth month, he was buried.
proposals.reason: The subject of 葬 after 孝惠帝崩 is Emperor Xiaohui (male), not the empress dowager.

proposals.before: She enfeoffed Zizhang, a son of King Daohui of Qi, as Marquis of Zhuxu and married Lu Lu's daughter to him.
proposals.after: She enfeoffed Zhang, a son of King Daohui of Qi, as Marquis of Zhuxu and married Lü Lu's daughter to him.
proposals.reason: In 子章, 子 means son and 章 is the given name; Zizhang incorrectly fuses kinship 子 into the name. Also 呂祿 is Lü Lu, not Lu Lu.

proposals.before: In the fourth year, she enfeoffed Lü Kui as Marquis of Linguang, Lü Ta as Marquis of Yu, Lü Gengshi as Marquis of Zhuiji, Lü Fen as Marquis of Lücheng, and also enfeoffed five chancellors as marquises.
proposals.after: In the fourth year, she enfeoffed Lü Xu as Marquis of Linguang, Lü Ta as Marquis of Yu, Lü Gengshi as Marquis of Zhuiji, Lü Fen as Marquis of Lücheng, and also enfeoffed five chancellors as marquises.
proposals.reason: 呂媭 is Lü Xu (Empress Lü's sister), not Lü Kui.

proposals.before: Empress Lü wished to make Lü clan kings. She first established Emperor Xiaohui's rear palace son Qiang as the King of Huaiyang, son Buyi as the King of Changshan, son Shan as Lord Xiangcheng, son Zhao as Lord Zhi, son Wu as Lord Huguan.
proposals.after: Empress Lü wished to make Lü clan kings. She first established Emperor Xiaohui's rear palace son Qiang as the King of Huaiyang, son Buyi as the King of Changshan, son Shan as Lord Xiangcheng, son Chao as Lord Zhi, son Wu as Lord Huguan.
proposals.reason: 子朝 is Chao (朝), not Zhao.

proposals.before: Some of his ministers secretly brought him food, but each time they were seized and punished. Starving, the King of Zhao sang, "The Lu clan rules, and the Liu house is in peril; they threaten kings and marquises, and force one of their women on me as consort.
proposals.after: Some of his ministers secretly brought him food, but each time they were seized and punished. Starving, the King of Zhao sang, "The Lü clan rules, and the Liu house is in peril; they threaten kings and marquises, and force one of their women on me as consort.
proposals.reason: 諸呂 is the Lü clan; Lu without umlaut confuses with 魯.

proposals.before: Empress Lü's younger sister Lü Kui had a daughter who was the wife of Lord Yingling Liu Ze. Ze was Grand General.
proposals.after: Empress Lü's younger sister Lü Xu had a daughter who was the wife of Lord Yingling Liu Ze. Ze was Grand General.
proposals.reason: 呂媭 is Lü Xu, not Lü Kui.

decisions.reason: 子 is the kinship word son in parallel with 其子呂臺; the given name is 產, not 子產. The chapter later explicitly has 呂產 and identifies him as Tai's younger brother (s0113). Chan repairs a false name without adding Chinese or an unnecessary full-name gloss.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 長兄周呂侯死事，封其子呂臺為酈侯，子產為交侯；

decisions.reason: The opening identifies Gaozu's eight sons. 子 in the parallel 子恢, 子友, 子長, 子建 is son, not part of each name. Later 王友 (s0029), 梁王恢 (s0132), and 燕靈王建 (s0150) confirm the shorter names. Preserve all other wording.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 餘皆孝惠弟，戚姬子如意為趙王，薄夫人子恒為代王，諸姬子子恢為梁王，子友為淮陽王，子長為淮南王，子建為燕王。

decisions.reason: Reject unnecessary rewording. 犁明 already means dawn, and 孝惠還 followed by 趙王已死 is accurately rendered by the existing two sentences. By dawn/had returned introduces an unnecessary deadline/pluperfect nuance rather than repairing a demonstrated fidelity error.

葬 continues the account beginning 孝惠帝崩 at s0053; the living empress dowager mourns him and continues governing. The buried person is Emperor Xiaohui, so he is correct. The literal field's impersonal burial took place is already accurate. No date conversion is approved.

齊悼惠王子章 means King Daohui's son Zhang, not a person named Zizhang. s0168 explicitly supplies 劉章. 呂祿 is the same Lü Lu already named at s0058; keep Lu for the given name 祿 and restore Lü only for the surname.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封齊悼惠王子章為朱虛侯，以呂祿女妻之。

decisions.reason: The source reads 呂媭. Shiji 095 calls Fan Kuai's wife and Empress Lü's younger sister 呂須, and the traditional Tongjian annotation reads 媭音須. Xu, not Kui, is supported; s0203 already uses Lü Xu. This decision changes only that erroneous reading, not the other offices/names in the sentence.

sourceWitness.citation: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/史記/卷095 (樊噲: 呂須; compare shiji/009 s0098, s0136, s0203, s0235)
sourceWitness.excerpt: 噲以呂后女弟呂須為婦，生子伉，故其比諸將最親。

decisions.reason: Reject as insufficiently evidenced in this review, not as proof that Zhao is uniquely correct. 朝 has both zhao and chao readings; the consulted primary text and Shiji annotations identify 子朝/軹侯朝 but supply no name-specific pronunciation ruling. Mere use of Chao in extraction metadata cannot independently establish error. Retain an explicit pronunciation hold for s0092/s0110/s0190.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太后欲王呂氏，先立孝惠後宮子彊為淮陽王，子不疑為常山王，子山為襄城侯，子朝為軹侯，子武為壺關侯。

decisions.reason: 諸呂 is the Lü clan, already distinguished chapterwide from 魯 (Lu) and the given name 祿 (Lu). Restore the existing surname spelling Lü in this occurrence; do not alter genuine King of Lu references or bare Lu for 祿. This is a one-letter name correction, not an inserted pinyin gloss.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其群臣或竊饋，輒捕論之，趙王餓，乃歌曰：「諸呂用事兮劉氏危，迫脅王侯兮彊授我妃。

decisions.reason: 女弟呂媭 is Empress Lü's younger sister. Shiji 095 independently writes 呂須 for this woman and identifies her as Fan Kuai's wife; the traditional pronunciation note is 媭音須. Replace Kui with Xu while preserving the daughter, marriage, title, and generalship wording.
